info.description:
# Connectum: platform API reference

One place for every API this project talks to or offers. Import this file and `Connectum.postman_environment.json` into Postman, pick the environment, fill the variables.

| Folder | What is in it |
|---|---|
| 1. Connectum REST | The HTTP endpoints of the backend: first-run setup, account sign-in (emailed code or password), finding / joining / entering an organisation, session, 2FA, admin unlock, public lookups, feed, files, Data Bin reports, and the calls other systems make (published API, people API). |
| 2. Consumer program | The three internal calls the consumer makes to the backend (Axpert session, record id report, send a record to a Put API). |
| 3. Axpert ARM API | Signin, ARMConnectToAxpert, ARMGetMenu, AxList, AxPut (validate, create, edit, grid probe, delete), AxGet: with what was learned on the real service. |
| 4. Connectum actions | All actions sent over the WebSocket (`/sd <action> {json}`), by area: who may call, arguments, reply, what it does. |
| 5. RabbitMQ management API | Queue depths, peeking at the failed queues. |

## How the system fits together

```
app (React) --WebSocket /sd actions + REST--> Connectum backend (Erlang, Redis)
backend --Redis stream sd:msgq--> bridge (Node) --RabbitMQ exchange connectum.data--> .NET consumer
consumer: queue connectum.messages -> managed database (messages, form records)
          queue connectum.axpert   -> AxPut into an Axpert tstruct (asks the backend for the person's session)
          queue connectum.rpc.requests <- backend's questions (who approves a step, who is told)
backend --ARM API--> Axpert (menu, fields, data sources); the person's sign-in is kept sealed
```

## Conventions

- Replies: `{ok:true, data}` or `{ok:false, error:{code, message, details?}}`. Field errors: `error.code = invalid_values`, `error.details.fields = {field: message}`.
- Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <session token>` (14-day session) from `POST /api/sd/login`. The WebSocket takes the same token as its first message.
- Names in the organisation lists are case-insensitive identities (the lower-cased trimmed name). The Redis keys are in `docs/CONNECTUM_API.md`.
- Secrets (passwords, tokens, the consumer secret) are never returned by any call and never logged.

## Regenerating this file

`node tools/postman/build.mjs` (from the connectum folder) rebuilds the collection, the environment and `docs/SD_ACTIONS_REFERENCE.md` from the backend source (levels, slow actions) and `tools/postman/actions-data.mjs` (descriptions). The build stops with a list if an action exists in the code but not in the table.

More detail: `docs/CONNECTUM_API.md` (the full API guide), `docs/RABBITMQ_CONSUMER_CONTRACT.md` (what is on the queues), `docs/CONSUMER_DOTNET_GUIDE.md` (the consumer), `docs/APPROVALS_NOTIFICATIONS_LOGIC.md`.

item.name: 3. Axpert ARM API
item.description:
The gateway in front of Axpert (`{{armBase}}`, e.g. https://agile.axi-global.com/ARM_API). Checked against the real service (erpgolddev, October 2026).

**Things that surprise people**
- Sign in with `password = md5(seed + md5(plain password))` and a `seed` you choose (the pre-request script of *Signin* does it). Sending the plain password fails.
- A session lasts **30 minutes** (the token's own expiry) and an Axpert user has **one session**: any new sign-in as that user ends the older one. `ClearPreviousSession:false` is refused with `duplicate_session`. Connectum signs in again by itself when it finds its session dead.
- Every later call sends BOTH the token (`Authorization: Bearer`) and the `ARMSessionId` (in the body).
- Replies are sometimes JSON inside a JSON string (`"{\"result\":...}"`), including errors: parse twice.
- AxList answers HTTP 200 (or 206 `partialsuccess`) even when a data source failed: look at `result.success` and at `result.data[0].error`.
- Run the requests in order: Signin, then ARMConnectToAxpert. The test script of Signin saves `armSessionId` and `armToken`.

**Learned later (October 2026, also checked on erpdemo)**
- The seed of the sign-in can be any text: `12345` works.
- **One transaction per AxPut call.** A call with several entries in `data` fails even when every entry is valid (`Index was out of range...`, `index: "1"`), and a refusal reports only the first failing one: `{message, index, transid, success:false}`. So send one entry per call. About 8 calls at once is the fastest (around 60 validate-only calls a second on the demo server; 16 is no faster).
- **Browsers may call the ARM API directly.** It answers with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` (the preflight too), so a web page can sign in and call it with no proxy.
- Data sources some projects have: `ds_tstruct_dc` (`transid`) gives the containers `{value, text, asgrid T/F, frmno}`; `ds_fields` (`transid`, `dcname` = comma separated containers) gives `{value, text, asgrid, frmno, datatype}`. `ds_tstructs` and `ds_field_mapping_memory` exist on erpdev and erpdemo but fail through AxList with `42601: syntax error at or near ";"` (their SQL probably ends with a `;`). `pagesize: 0` returns every row. The list of structures can be taken from ARMGetMenu instead (`PageTs<id>`).
- Editing a record that does not exist, or that the user may not edit, answers `User does not have permissions to edit this record.` (also with `validateonly`).

Dates `yyyy-MM-dd`, times like `04:04 AM`, a check box `T`/`F`, a multi-choice comma separated.

Edits the record named by `keyfield:"recordid"` and `keyvalue` (**as text**, not a number: a number is refused). Verified: it targets exactly that record even when another has the same key value.

item.name: AxPut: probe whether a container is a grid

request.description: Axpert's field metadata does not say which containers are grids, but this does: two FILLED rows in a container that is not a grid are refused with `Cannot create new row in Non-grid DC 1 as already a row exists`; a grid takes both (and complains about what is missing). Empty rows are skipped by Axpert, so the rows must carry a value. `validateonly:true`: nothing is saved. Connectum uses this for `axpert.fields`.

AxPut has no delete: `Invalid action - DELETE.` A row action `axrow_action:"delete"` on the header container answers `DC rows using same table as Header DC can't be deleted.` So a record deleted in Connectum stays in Axpert.
Reads one record (from the Axpert ARM handbook; not used by Connectum yet). A user without access to the structure gets `User does not have access to this structure.`

item.name: 4. Connectum actions over the WebSocket (reference)
item.description: All 330 actions, by area. Level: none = any open connection; user = any signed-in person; host = a host; manage = an administrator or a person allowed to manage users; admin = an administrator (admin console unlocked in strict mode); test = test only.

item.name: How to call an action (read this first)

request.description:
Actions are sent over the WebSocket, which Postman collections cannot hold. Three ways to call one:

**1. Postman's own WebSocket request** (New > WebSocket): connect to `{{wsUrl}}`, send `{"username":"{{username}}","token":"{{token}}","armSessionId":"any-text"}` (wait for `{"type":"welcome"}`), then send text messages like:
`/sd tstruct.get {"name":"leave_request","reqId":1}`
The reply: `{"type":"sd","reqId":1,"ok":true,"data":{...}}` or `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"...","message":"..."}}`. `reqId` is any value you choose; it is echoed back. Server events arrive as `{"type":"sd_event","event":"...","data":{...}}`.

**2. The command line** (Node 22): `WS=ws://localhost:8080 USERNAME=root TOKEN=... node tools/postman/sd-call.mjs me` or `... tstruct.get '{"name":"leave_request"}'`.

**3. The browser console of the running app**: the app's own client (`form-studio/src/core/api.js`, method `sd(action, args)`).

Get the token with *Sign in* and then *Enter the organisation* in folder 1. Strict mode: administrators must unlock the admin console first (`admin.unlock.start`, `admin.unlock`). A rate limit applies (CHAT_RATE_LIMIT_MAX); a limited call still gets a reply with its `reqId`.

The requests in the sub-folders below send `GET /api/sd/session` (a harmless call that proves your token works); their DESCRIPTION is the reference for the area. The same tables are in `docs/SD_ACTIONS_REFERENCE.md`.

Who am I, my profile, my settings.

| Action | Who | Arguments | Reply | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `me` | none | `{}` | `{user, mode, feed, ...}` | Who the connection is: the signed-in user, the mode (open or strict) and counters. Works on any open connection. |
| `profile.get` | user | `{}` | `{profile}` | Everything about me: address, gender, date of birth, education, skills, roles. |
| `profile.update` | user | `{address?, gender?, dob?, education?, skills?, city?, country?, pin?}` | `{profile}` | Change my own profile. Nothing else can be changed here. |
| `settings.get` | user | `{}` | `{settings:{themeMode, globalChatColorId, chatColorOverrides, liquidGlass, updated}}` | My saved theme and chat colours (kept on the server so every device agrees). |
| `settings.save` | user | `{themeMode?, globalChatColorId?, chatColorOverrides?, liquidGlass?}` | `{settings}` | Save settings. Only what is sent changes. |
| `settings.reset` | user | `{}` | `{settings}` | Back to the defaults. |
| `formlayout.get` | user | `{name}` | `{name, layout\|null}` | My own arrangement of a form (order of fields, sections, grid columns). null = the form's own order. |
| `formlayout.save` | user | `{name, layout:{fields?, sections?, columns?}}` | `{name, layout}` | Keep my arrangement of a form. An empty layout is a reset. |
| `formlayout.reset` | user | `{name}` | `{name, layout:null}` | Back to the form's own order. |
| `permissions.mine` | user | `{}` | `{permissions, known, onboardsEmployees, canInviteEmployees}` | What my roles allow (broadcast, register affiliates, invite customers/suppliers) and whether I may invite employees. |
| `connect.my` | user | `{}` | `{person:{code, display, payload, url, name, username}, enterprise:{...card...}}` | My personal connect code (for the QR) and the enterprise card. The person's payload names the organisation: <address>/connect/<CODE>?org=<ENTERPRISE CODE>; the organisation's own does not. |
| `connect.rotate` | user | `{}` | `{person}` | A new personal code; the old one stops working. |
| `connect.scan` | user | `{code}` | `{associated \| enterprise}` | Scan a code. A personal code makes the two of you associates at once; an enterprise code returns its card. The code may be the whole link, connectum:CODE, <scheme>://connect/CODE or CODE?org=.. (with ?org= and ?branch=). A link that names another organisation than this one is refused: wrong_org. |
| `connect.lookup` | user | `{code}` | `{enterprise \| person}` | What a code belongs to, without connecting. Reads the same link forms as connect.scan; a link for another organisation answers wrong_org. |
| `e2e.status` | user | `{id?}` | `{mode, devices (each with `late`), maxDevices, recovery}` | End-to-end encryption: the mode, which of my devices are registered (the recovery key, when there is one, is listed with `recovery: true` and the label Recovery key), and whether recovery is on. Naming this device with `id` tells the server it is still in use. |
| `e2e.register` | user | `{id (32 hex), ecdh, sign, proof, label?}` | `{device}` | Register this device: its ECDH and signing public keys (P-256, base64url) and the proof of the signing key. 30 registrations an hour. |
| `e2e.remove` | user | `{id}` | `{removed}` | Remove one of my device keys. The recovery key is refused (`invalid`: turn recovery off instead). |
| `e2e.recovery.set` | user | `{id (32 hex), ecdh, sign, proof, blob:{v:1, salt, iv, ct}, replace?}` | `{device}` | Turn recovery on: register a recovery key (one more device of mine, flagged `recovery`, that every message is then also wrapped for) and keep its private half sealed with a code only the person has (the server cannot open it). Same proof as a device. `replace: true` makes a new one when recovery is already on (`conflict` otherwise). 10 an hour. See docs/E2E_ENCRYPTION.md section 6a. |
| `e2e.recovery.get` | user | `{}` | `{recovery:false} or {recovery:true, id, ecdh, sign, blob}` | The sealed recovery key, for the signed-in person only: a new browser or phone opens it with the code, then can read what was sent after recovery was turned on. 30 an hour. |
| `e2e.recovery.delete` | user | `{}` | `{removed}` | Turn recovery off: removes the recovery key and the sealed copy. `not_found` when it was not on. |
| `e2e.sync.pending` | user | `{}` | `{waiting:[{id,label,ts}], helpers:[{id,label,ts,seen?}], recovery: null \| {id, backedUp}}` | History for a new device: which of my devices are still waiting to be shown the earlier messages (added after another one existed), and which devices could show them (not waiting). Both lists only count devices used in the last 30 days, so a browser that lost its keys is not offered again and again. The recovery key is never in those two lists; `recovery` says where its backup stands (`backedUp: false` until the past has been locked for it). |
| `e2e.sync.page` | user | `{cursor?}` | `{items:[{id,text}], next}` | My own encrypted messages, direct chats and groups I am in, newest first within each chat (what I cleared stays cleared; deleted messages are left out), each envelope narrowed to my own boxes. A page ends after the store page that reaches the limit; follow `next` (opaque, null at the end). 600 calls per 10 minutes. |
| `e2e.sync.put` | user | `{device, items:[{mid, iv, w, ek}] (1..500)}` | `{stored}` | Boxes for the past, made by one of my devices for one of my own devices: a device waiting to be shown the past, or the recovery key (that is the backup). Stored next to the message id and added to the envelope, for that device only, when it is served. `not_found` for a device that is not mine, `invalid` for a malformed item. 400 calls per 10 minutes. |
| `e2e.sync.done` | user | `{device}` | `{done}` | My device says it has finished showing the past to `device`: it stops waiting (for the recovery key: the backup is complete). My other devices are told (`e2e_devices_changed`). |
| `e2e.devices` | user | `{users:[usernames] (1..50)}` | `{devices:{username:[device]}}` | The public device keys of the people I may message (to encrypt a direct message to them). |
| `e2e.group_devices` | user | `{group}` | `{members:[{user, devices}]}` | The device keys of every member of a group. |
| `test.sleep` | test | `{ms}` | `{slept}` | Test only (CONNECTUM_TEST_ACTIONS=1): sleeps; proves a slow action never blocks the connection. |
| `test.slow_sleep` | test, slow | `{ms}` | `{slept}` | Test only: the same, on the slow-action lane. |
| `test.conv.queue` | test | `{}` | `{pending, dead, stats}` | Test only: what the background conversation clean-ups are holding. |
| `test.mail.queue` | test | `{}` | `{pending, dead, counts}` | Test only: the mail waiting to be sent, and what failed. |
| `test.convpurge.poison` | test | `{}` | `-` | Test only: queues a poisoned conversation-clean-up job. |

Contacts, hosts, requests, approvals, conversations.

| Action | Who | Arguments | Reply | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `assoc.list` | user | `{}` | `{associates:[{user, relation: host\|user\|peer, online}]}` | My contact list: the people I am connected to, and what they are to me. |
| `assoc.invite` | user | `{to}` | `{request}` | Ask someone to connect (a peer link). They must accept. |
| `assoc.handover` | user | `{person, to}` | `{request}` | Employees/admins: hand a person I am connected with (a patient, a customer) over to another employee. The person is asked first. |
| `assoc.remove` | user | `{user}` | `{removed}` | Remove a peer link. |
| `care.thread` | user | `{person}` | `{conversation, person}` | The id of the shared care conversation with a person (not_found if there is none). |
| `record.thread` | user | `{id}` | `{conversation, id, title}` | The id and title of one record's own conversation, for a structure with recordThread on (the person who saved it, the people it names, administrators; not_found otherwise). Made on first ask for a record saved before the switch was on. |
| `record.names` | user | `{}` | `{names, canRename, hidden}` | The titles of the record conversations I am in, by group name ("rec-ticket-12": "Ticket #12: printer is down"), which of them I may rename (the ones whose record I saved), and which the structure keeps out of the main chat list (recordThreadInList off). |
| `record.rename` | user | `{id, name}` | `{id, title}` | Rename one record's conversation for everyone in it. Only the person who saved the record may (forbidden otherwise); an empty name brings the made title back. At most 60 characters. |
| `users.search` | user | `{q}` | `{users:[{username, name, designation, designations, department, branch, affiliate, category, isEmployee, isHost, status, canInteract, connected, canMessage, avatar}]}` | Find people (at most 20; not yourself, not deactivated people). Strict mode: exact username, email or mobile only. canInteract: the interaction rules allow it; connected: already linked; canMessage: a direct message would be accepted now; avatar: the picture address or null. |
| `users.colleagues` | user | `{q?, limit?, after?}` | `{people:[{username, name, designation, department, branch, avatar, connected, online}], hasMore, next}` | The people I may add to a group, online or not, A to Z by name. Employees and administrators browse the whole organisation; anyone else sees only the people they are tied to. q narrows by name, username, designation or department; limit is at most 50; pass `next` back as `after` for the next page. No email or mobile is returned. |
| `users.invite` | user | `{name, email, mobile?, isEmployee?, branch?, department?, designation?, designations?, reportingManager?, employeeCode?, category?, roles?, isHost?, hostScope?}` | `{user}` | Invite one person. Administrators and hosts invite anyone in their scope; an employee whose designation may onboard invites those employees; a role may allow inviting customers/suppliers. |
| `users.resend_invite` | user | `{username}` | `{sent, to}` | Send the invitation again to someone who has not signed in yet (once a minute). |
| `hosts.mine` | user | `{}` | `{hosts:[...]}` | The hosts that cover me. |
| `host.users` | host | `{}` | `{users:[...]}` | Host: the people I host. |
| `host.transfer` | user | `{user, toHost}` | `{request}` | Host: hand one of my people to another host (the other host is asked). |
| `req.list` | user | `{status?, limit?, offset?}` | `{requests, total, offset, limit, hasMore}` | My requests: approvals to answer, connection requests, handovers. Default status is pending; `all` or a status. Each has `direction` (incoming, outgoing, other) and `canRespond`: show Approve and Decline only when it is true. Nobody answers their own request, an administrator included (unless no one else could), so `canRespond` is false for the sender. An answered request also carries `resolvedBy`, `resolvedByName` and `resolvedByDesignation` (the designation of the person who answered, null when they have none). |
| `req.respond` | user | `{id, action: accept\|reject\|return\|ignore, reason?, allowResubmit?, comment?}` | `{request}` | Answer a request. Declining a submission can allow the author to fix and resend it. Answering your own request is refused (`forbidden`: You sent this request, so it is waiting for ...), also for an administrator. |
| `conv.list` | user | `{full?}` | `{conversations:[...]}` | {}: the conversations I have a state for (archived, deleted, pinned, muted, read). {full:true}: EVERY conversation (direct, groups, general room) with lastId, readId, unread (at most 99, unreadMore), pinned, muted, and for a direct one peerReadId, peerDeliveredId and the other person's avatar. |
| `conv.pin` | user | `{id}` | `{conversation}` | Pin a conversation for me (kept on the server). Idempotent. conv.unpin undoes it. |
| `conv.unpin` | user | `{id}` | `{conversation}` | Unpin a conversation for me. Idempotent. |
| `conv.mute` | user | `{id}` | `{conversation}` | Mute a conversation for me (a flag: the app decides what quiet means). Idempotent. conv.unmute undoes it. |
| `conv.unmute` | user | `{id}` | `{conversation}` | Unmute a conversation for me. Idempotent. |
| `conv.read` | user | `{id, upTo?}` | `{conversation}` | I have read up to that message (default: everything now). Only moves forward, clamped to the newest. The other person of a direct conversation gets a receipt event and later reads peerReadId. |
| `conv.delivered` | user | `{id, upTo?}` | `{conversation}` | My device has received up to that message (the sender's delivery tick). Reading implies it. |
| `conv.readers` | user | `{id:"group:<name>", messageId}` | `{messageId, total, readCount, readers:[{user, readTs}]}` | Who of the group has read my message. Only its author may ask. |
| `conv.unread` | user | `{id, messageId}` | `{conversation}` | Mark the conversation unread from that message on (my own view only: nothing the other people see changes). The conversation then has `unreadFrom` (a message id) and `unread` counts from there; the next `conv.read` clears it. |
| `msg.save` | user | `{conv, id}` | `{saved:true}` | Save a message for myself (`conv` is "dm:<user>", "group:<name>" or "global"). At most 500 per person (`limit`). Saving again changes nothing. Other devices get `saved_changed`. |
| `msg.unsave` | user | `{id}` | `{saved:false}` | Take a message off my saved list (fine if it is not on it). |
| `msg.saved` | user | `{ids?, limit?, offset?}` | `{items:[{id, conv, from, text, ts, kind, savedTs}], total, limit, offset} or {ids:[...]}` | My saved messages, newest saved first, the text narrowed to my own end-to-end boxes. `ids:true` returns only the ids (to mark them in a chat). A message deleted for everyone leaves the list; one I cleared is not shown. |
| `msg.pin` | user | `{conv, id}` | `{pinned:true, count}` | Pin a message for everyone in a direct chat or a group (either person, or any member). At most 10 per conversation (`limit`); not in the general room. Everyone in the conversation gets `pins_changed`. |
| `msg.unpin` | user | `{conv, id}` | `{pinned:false, count}` | Unpin it (anyone in the conversation may). |
| `msg.pins` | user | `{conv}` | `{pins:[{id, by, ts, message:{id, conv, from, text, ts, kind}}], max}` | The pinned messages of a conversation, newest pin first. |
| `conv.archive` | user | `{id}` | `{conversation}` | Archive a conversation (idempotent). |
| `conv.unarchive` | user | `{id}` | `{conversation}` | Bring it back. |
| `conv.delete` | user | `{id}` | `{conversation, purge}` | Delete for me: hidden at once; the history is cleaned in the background. |
| `forms.forward` | user | `{id, chats:[chat id]}` | `{results}` | Forward a submitted form (as a message) into other conversations. |
| `interaction.mine` | user | `{}` | `{designation, interactWith, affiliate?}` | What my own interaction rule says: which designations I may deal with (null = everyone). |
| `interaction.allowed` | user | `{user}` | `{allowed, reason?}` | May I deal with that person? |
| `affiliate.register` | user | `{name, category, country?, city?, pin?, branches?}` | `{affiliate}` | Register an affiliate organisation (needs the register_affiliate role permission). Gets a number like AFF-000001. |
| `affiliate.list` | user | `{q?}` | `{affiliates:[{name, number, category, city, country}]}` | Employees: search affiliates. |
| `onboarding.get` | user | `{category}` | `{process}` | The onboarding process of a user category (public to a signed-in person). |

The right-hand panel.

Defining and filling forms, the options that open them.

| Action | Who | Arguments | Reply | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `options.list` | user | `{}` | `{options:[{id, caption, type, category, target, targetScope, display, order, owner}]}` | The options I may see (an option's 'applicable to' rules decide). These are the Smart Prompts. |
| `options.categories` | user | `{}` | `{categories:[{id, label, icon, types, executable, count}], total}` | One entry per Smart Prompts pill, with how many options I have in it. |
| `option.run` | user, slow | `{id, ...}` | `{open \| url \| ...}` | Run an option: open a form, an Axpert item, the catalog, start a payment ... The reply says what the app should do. not_configured when the option has nothing to open. |
| `tstruct.get` | user | `{name}` | `{tstruct, rev}` | A form definition, if one of my options points at it. Fields with a `source` come with the current names as `options`. `rev` is a short fingerprint of the saved definition (not of those current names): it changes when the form is changed, so an app drops what it kept for the form when its rev differs. |
| `tstruct.submit` | user | `{name, values:{field: value}, ref?, meta?, cid?}` | `{submission, recordStatus, cid?, duplicate?}` | Fill in a form. cid (a client id, 1 to 64 characters: letters, digits, - _ . :) makes a retry safe: the same id again returns the first answer with duplicate:true and saves nothing (remembered a day, per person). recordStatus is saved, or pending when it needs approval. Setup forms also make the real change (result on the submission). Send the value of every shown field, and of every hidden field whose value is made for the person (an auto value, a fill); what is sent for any other hidden field is ignored. |
| `form.inherit` | user | `{tstruct, scope?, values}` | `{values:{Field:Value}, locked:[Field]}` | What the fields that start from the record chosen in a Drop Down are now (locked unless an Override switch says Yes). |
| `form.options` | user, slow | `{tstruct, scope?, field, values?, search?, limit?, offset?, ifNoneMatch?}` | `{options:[{value,label}], columns, rows, total, truncated, cached, waiting, etag, cacheSec} or {notModified:true, etag, cacheSec}` | What a Selection field with a data source offers. Whoever may open the form may read it. waiting = a field it depends on is empty. `etag` fingerprints the choices and `cacheSec` is how long the server keeps this source's answer (an API or data source says so itself; 0 for Connectum's own forms): an app keeps its copy for no longer than that, and sends the etag back as `ifNoneMatch` to be told `notModified` (no choices) while nothing changed. No etag while `waiting`. |
| `submissions.list` | user | `{tstruct?, ref?, recordsOnly?, limit?, offset?}` | `{submissions, total, offset, limit, hasMore}` | My submissions plus those of the people I host. |
| `submission.get` | user | `{id}` | `{submission}` | One submission I may open (author, host, admin, an approver, a notified designation). |
| `submissions.update` | user | `{id, values?, meta?}` | `{submission}` | The author edits a submission (not while it waits for approval). Re-checked against the form; Auto Generate numbers are kept. |
| `submission.resubmit` | user | `{id, values?, meta?}` | `{submission}` | The author fixes a declined submission (if the approver allowed it) and sends it again. |
| `submissions.delete` | user | `{id}` | `{deleted}` | The author deletes a submission. |
| `records.list` | user | `{tstruct, q?, from?, to?, scope?: mine\|all, limit? (1..100, 20), offset?}` | `{records, total, ...}` | Records of one form, newest first, searchable as text (looks at the newest 1000 I may see). Waiting or declined submissions are not records. |
| `tstruct.user.list` | user | `{}` | `{tstructs}` | Forms people made themselves (visible to everyone). |
| `tstruct.user.get` | user | `{name}` | `{tstruct}` | One user-made form. |
| `tstruct.user.save` | user | `{name, caption?, description?, fields[], sections[], approval?, notify?, saveToDb?, axpert?}` | `{tstruct}` | Create a form of my own. `duplicate` if the name is taken. An Axpert target is checked with MY Axpert connection. |
| `tstruct.user.update` | user | `{same body}` | `{tstruct}` | Edit my form (creator only). |
| `tstruct.user.delete` | user | `{name}` | `{deleted}` | Delete my form (creator only). Records are kept. |
| `tstruct.user.open` | user | `{name}` | `{tstruct}` | Open a user-made form for filling. |
| `tstruct.user.submit` | user | `{name, values, ref?, meta?}` | `{submission}` | Fill in a user-made form. |
| `option.user.list` | user | `{}` | `{options, types}` | The options I made (an administrator gets all). |
| `option.user.save` | user | `{id?, caption, type, target?, display?, applicable?, active?, order?}` | `{option}` | Create or edit an option of my own. |
| `option.user.delete` | user | `{id}` | `{deleted}` | Delete one (creator or administrator). |
| `cfg.lookups` | user | `{}` | `{branches, departments, designations, roles, categories, ...}` | The organisation's lists as names, for pickers (any signed-in person). |
| `admin.tstruct.list` | admin | `{}` | `{tstructs}` | Admin: every admin-made form definition. |
| `admin.tstruct.get` | admin | `{name}` | `{tstruct}` | Admin: one definition. |
| `admin.tstruct.save` | admin | `{name, caption?, description?, fields[], sections[], approval?:{enabled, stages\|designations}, notify?, allowForward?, saveToDb?, axpert?:{app, transid, gridDcs?, defaults?}}` | `{tstruct}` | Admin: create or update a form. Field types: text, date, time, wholenumber, number, email, url, mobile, location, list, selection, fill, barcode, autogenerate. See CONNECTUM_API.md. A field may be hidden (`hidden: true`): for an ordinary field the person does not see it and whatever is sent for it is ignored (its default, if any, is saved); for a field whose value is made for the person (`calc`, `fetch`, an Auto Generate number) hidden only keeps it off the screen: its value is still worked out, sent, checked and saved, so a client must send it. A hidden field that fills from an API or another form and is required needs a default value; an auto value is never required; a hidden auto column in a grid section is refused by the builder. |
| `admin.tstruct.delete` | admin | `{name}` | `{deleted}` | Admin: delete a form (refused with in_use while an option opens it). |
| `admin.option.list` | admin | `{}` | `{options, types}` | Admin: all options. |
| `admin.option.save` | admin | `{id, caption, type, target?, display?, applicable?, adminOnly?, condition?, active?, order?}` | `{option}` | Admin: create or update an option. Types: data_input (a structure), get_data (a List API or data source), link (target = a link id), page (target = a published page id; only with the Code Studio plugin), download, upload, catalog, pay, axpert_tstruct, axpert_smartview, axpert_iview, axpert_page. `adminOnly` hides it from everyone but administrators. |
| `admin.option.delete` | admin | `{id}` | `{deleted}` | Admin: delete an option. |
| `admin.packs.list` | admin | `{}` | `{packs:[{id, title, description, forms, options, installed}]}` | Admin: the ready-made packs (hospital, college, customers, hr, purchase, sales, employee, candidates, suppliers, setup). |
| `admin.packs.install` | admin | `{pack}` | `{pack, created, skipped}` | Admin: install a pack. Never overwrites: existing names are skipped. |
| `care.names` | user | `{}` | `{...}` | The shared-thread titles for the person's care threads. |
